theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas leads the ranks by a wide margin (1.317) and is eligible, but the underlying texture is fragile: durability_bar is only 0.41, hurst_tag is 'mean-revert', and breadth is 0.0 — meaning the score is concentrated in a single name or extremely narrow leadership, not a broad sector bid. A mean-revert tag on the top-ranked theme signals elevated shake-out risk even if the absolute-trend gate (the one validated edge) currently holds. This is a caution against chasing the leader, not a fade call.
theses.dissent: Energy can trend hard on supply shocks or geopolitical risk premiums, and the absolute-trend gate still shows eligibility. If oil breaks out on a real supply disruption, the narrow breadth could widen quickly and the mean-revert tag would flip. Avoiding the leader could mean missing the strongest directional move in the market.

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Consumer Staples & Retail is the only top-3 theme with a 'trend' hurst tag, full breadth (1.0), and a high durability bar (0.8), yet it is flagged crowded (crowding_z 1.02). The crowding flag is a size-down caution only, not a fade signal. The structural read is that the trend is broad and cohesive — the kind of setup the absolute-trend gate is designed to hold through shake-outs. Momentum rank 3 reflects focus, not a return forecast.
theses.dissent: The crowding flag is real: staples and retail being the full-breadth trend while the leader is fragile suggests late-cycle defensive positioning that could unwind rapidly if risk appetite returns. A crowded trend with rank 3 may have already priced in most of the move, leaving low upside and sharp downside on any rotation back to cyclicals.
